column1: Title
column5: Preconditions
column6: Steps
column7: Expected Result

column1: Verify the whole-work-order Add Fee/Discount dialog opens from the work order more (⋯) menu
column5:
1. You are logged in as a role that has Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open (not Invoiced, not Paid) work order exists; you are viewing it and are not in history view.
3. You are on the work order's Lines tab.
column6:
1. At the top right of the Lines area, click the ⋯ (more) button next to 'New Line'.
2. In the menu that opens, click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
3. Look at the dialog that opens.
column7:
1. A dialog titled 'Add new fee/discount' opens.
2. There is no 'Applying to' line, because this fee/discount applies to the whole work order.
3. There is no scope dropdown to change — the dialog always applies to the whole work order.

column1: Verify adding a whole-work-order flat-amount fee saves and shows a success message
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order is open on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Open the ⋯ (more) menu at the top right of the Lines tab and click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. In the 'Name' field, type 'ZZAUTOTEST Handling Fee'.
3. Leave 'Type' set to 'Fee'.
4. Leave 'Calculation Type' set to 'Flat Amount'.
5. In the '$ Amount' field, enter 100.
6. Click the 'Add Fee' button.
column7:
1. While 'Flat Amount' is selected, the amount field is labelled '$ Amount' (a dollar amount).
2. The 'Add Fee' button can be used once Name, Type, Calculation Type and an amount above 0 are all filled in.
3. The dialog closes and a success message confirms the fee was added.
4. 'ZZAUTOTEST Handling Fee' now appears in the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card on the left, showing +$100.00.
5. The work order Subtotal and Total go up by $100.00 (tax is recalculated when you save).

column1: Verify the live preview shows a whole-work-order percentage discount before you save
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a Subtotal of $10,715.39 is open.
column6:
1. Open 'Add Fee/Discount' from the ⋯ menu on the Lines tab.
2. Set 'Type' to 'Discount'.
3. Set 'Calculation Type' to '% of Subtotal'.
4. In the 'Percent %' field, enter 8.
5. Read the preview box near the bottom of the dialog.
column7:
1. The preview works the discount out from the current Subtotal: 8% of $10,715.39 = −$857.23.
2. The preview shows the new work-order total after the discount ($9,858.16).
3. The preview reminds you that tax is recalculated when you save.
4. The discount is shown as a negative amount.

column1: Verify 'Apply From Template' fills the dialog with a template's values
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order is open; the location has at least one fee/discount template (for example a 'Fleet Standard Discount').
column6:
1. Open 'Add Fee/Discount' from the ⋯ menu.
2. Open the 'Apply From Template' dropdown at the top of the dialog.
3. Choose a template.
4. Look at the Name, Type, Calculation Type and amount fields.
column7:
1. Name is filled with the template's name.
2. Type is set to match the template (Fee or Discount).
3. Calculation Type is set to match the template.
4. The amount (and Max Amount, if the template has one) are filled from the template.
5. The fee/discount still applies to the whole work order (a template does not carry a scope).
6. The confirm button ('Add Fee' or 'Add Discount') can now be used.

column1: Verify the Add button stays disabled until Name, Type, Calculation Type and an Amount above 0 are all filled in
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. The 'Add new fee/discount' dialog is freshly open with all fields blank.
column6:
1. With every field blank, look at the 'Add Fee' button.
2. Type a Name only, then look at the button.
3. Set Type to 'Fee', then look at the button.
4. Set Calculation Type to 'Flat Amount' (no amount yet), then look at the button.
5. Enter 0 in the '$ Amount' field, then look at the button.
6. Change the amount to 25, then look at the button.
column7:
1. With every field blank, the 'Add Fee' button is greyed out and cannot be used.
2. With only a Name, the button is still greyed out.
3. With Name and Type, the button is still greyed out.
4. With Name, Type and Calculation Type but no amount, the button is still greyed out.
5. With the amount set to 0, the button is still greyed out (the amount must be more than 0).
6. With the amount at 25 and everything else filled in, the button becomes usable. Max Amount is not required.

column1: Verify Max Amount caps a percentage fee (20% on a $100 base with Max Amount $15 → +$15.00)
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order whose base for the fee is $100.00 is open.
column6:
1. Open 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Set 'Type' to 'Fee' and 'Calculation Type' to a percentage method (for example '% of Subtotal').
3. In the 'Percent %' field, enter 20.
4. In the '$ Max Amount (Optional)' field, enter 15.
5. Read the preview, then click 'Add Fee'.
column7:
1. Without a cap the fee would be $20.00 (20% of $100).
2. Because Max Amount is $15.00, the fee is limited to +$15.00.
3. The saved fee shows +$15.00.

column1: Verify the confirm button label follows the Type (Add Fee vs Add Discount)
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. The 'Add new fee/discount' dialog is open.
column6:
1. Set 'Type' to 'Fee' and read the confirm button.
2. Change 'Type' to 'Discount' and read the confirm button again.
column7:
1. With Type set to 'Fee', the confirm button reads 'Add Fee'.
2. With Type set to 'Discount', the confirm button reads 'Add Discount' — the label changes as you change Type.

column1: Verify an empty Name blocks saving a whole-work-order fee/discount
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. The 'Add new fee/discount' dialog is open.
column6:
1. Leave the 'Name' field blank.
2. Set 'Type' to 'Fee', 'Calculation Type' to 'Flat Amount', and '$ Amount' to 10.
3. Try to save with 'Add Fee'.
column7:
1. The fee cannot be saved while the Name is blank.
2. A message tells you a Name is required.

column1: Verify an empty or zero amount blocks saving a whole-work-order fee/discount
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. The 'Add new fee/discount' dialog is open with a Name, Type 'Fee' and Calculation Type 'Flat Amount' set.
column6:
1. Leave '$ Amount' empty and try to save with 'Add Fee'.
2. Enter 0 in '$ Amount' and try to save again.
column7:
1. With the amount empty, the fee cannot be saved.
2. With the amount at 0, the fee cannot be saved — the amount must be more than 0 (the smallest flat amount is $0.01 and the smallest percentage is 0.01%).

column1: Verify a percentage discount over 100% is rejected while a percentage fee has no upper limit
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. The 'Add new fee/discount' dialog is open.
column6:
1. Set 'Type' to 'Discount', 'Calculation Type' to '% of Subtotal', 'Percent %' to 150, and try to save with 'Add Discount'.
2. Change 'Type' to 'Fee', keep the percentage method, set 'Percent %' to 150, and try to save with 'Add Fee'.
column7:
1. A 150% discount is rejected — a percentage discount cannot be more than 100%.
2. A 150% fee is accepted — percentage fees have no upper limit.

column1: Verify a whole-work-order percentage method uses the correct base (% of Subtotal example)
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with Labor $200.00, Parts $100.00, Shop Supplies $0.00 (so Subtotal = $300.00) and no other fees/discounts.
column6:
1. Open 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Open the 'Calculation Type' dropdown and read the options.
3. Set 'Type' to 'Fee', 'Calculation Type' to '% of Subtotal', 'Percent %' to 10.
4. Read the preview, then save with 'Add Fee'.
column7:
1. The Calculation Type dropdown offers exactly: 'Flat Amount', '% of Labor Total', '% of Parts Total', '% of Subtotal'.
2. '% of Subtotal' is worked out from Labor + Parts + Shop Supplies = $300.00.
3. 10% of $300.00 = +$30.00; the saved fee shows +$30.00.
4. There is no '% of Grand Total' option (that is only for Processing Fees).

column1: Verify Add Fee/Discount is hidden and blocked on an Invoiced or Paid work order
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. A work order in Invoiced (or Paid) status is open.
column6:
1. Open the work order ⋯ menu and look for 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Hover a labor line and a part row and look for their add fee/discount option.
column7:
1. 'Add Fee/Discount' is not shown in the ⋯ menu.
2. The labor-line and part-row add fee/discount options are not shown either.
3. A fee/discount cannot be added to an invoiced or paid work order by any route.

column1: Verify the whole-work-order Add Fee/Discount option is hidden without Work Orders: Create & Edit
column5:
1. You are logged in as a role that HAS See Financial Data but does NOT have Work Orders: Create & Edit.
2. An open work order is open.
column6: 1. Open the work order ⋯ menu and look for 'Add Fee/Discount'.
column7:
1. 'Add Fee/Discount' is not shown.
2. Existing whole-work-order fee/discount amounts are still visible (See Financial Data is on) but have no edit or delete controls.

column1: Verify the preview shows the empty-amount prompt before an amount is entered
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. The 'Add new fee/discount' dialog is freshly open.
column6:
1. Set 'Type' and 'Calculation Type' but leave the amount empty.
2. Read the preview box.
column7: 1. The preview box reads exactly: 'Enter an amount to see the impact.'

column1: Verify the preview amount is signed for a fee (+) vs a discount (−)
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. The 'Add new fee/discount' dialog is open.
column6:
1. Set 'Type' to 'Fee', 'Calculation Type' to 'Flat Amount', '$ Amount' to 50, and look at the preview amount.
2. Change 'Type' to 'Discount' and look at the preview amount again.
column7:
1. A fee shows as a positive amount with a '+' sign.
2. A discount shows as a negative amount with a '−' sign; the preview updates as you change the Type.

column1: Verify the Add/Edit fee-or-discount dialog shows the tax-jurisdiction note below the Taxable toggle
column5:
1. An open work order (not Invoiced/Paid, not in history view). Mark any throwaway data ZZAUTOTEST.
2. You can add a fee/discount (Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data).
column6:
1. Open 'Add Fee/Discount' from the work order ⋯ menu.
2. Look directly below the 'Taxable' Yes/No toggle for a note.
3. Open an existing fee/discount's Edit dialog and check the same place below the Taxable toggle.
column7:
1. Directly below the Taxable toggle this note is shown: 'Tax treatment varies by jurisdiction — confirm your local requirements before saving.'
2. The same note shows in both the Add and the Edit dialog.
3. The note is plain advice to the shop, not a system instruction and not a legal statement.
4. The note is shown only to users with See Financial Data — a user without See Financial Data does not see the note. (A user without See Financial Data cannot open this work-order Add/Edit dialog at all; the no-note side is observable in the admin Fee/Discount template dialog, opened by a user with Manage Finance Settings but without See Financial Data.)

column1: Verify a labor line's ⋮ menu opens the Add Fee/Discount dialog locked to that labor line
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line, e.g. Line 1 'Service - Perform LOF and inspection', is open on the Lines tab.
column6:
1. Hover the labor line row to show its ⋮ (more) button.
2. Click the ⋮ button and click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
3. Read the dialog title and subtitle.
column7:
1. The dialog 'Add new fee/discount' opens, locked to that labor line.
2. A grey subtitle reads 'Applying to: <line name>' (just the line name, no 'Line N Labor' prefix).
3. The scope cannot be changed inside the dialog.

column1: Verify a labor-line '% of Labor Total' fee works out against the line's labor price (10% of $150.00 → +$15.00)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line whose gross labor price is exactly $150.00, no existing adjustments on that line.
column6:
1. Open the labor line's ⋮ menu and click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Confirm the Calculation Type defaults to '% of Labor Total'.
3. Set Type 'Fee', 'Percent %' 10.
4. Read the preview, then save with 'Add Fee'.
column7:
1. The only methods offered are 'Flat Amount' and '% of Labor Total'.
2. The base is the labor line price = $150.00.
3. 10% of $150.00 = +$15.00.
4. The preview shows the line's labor total and the new line labor total.

column1: Verify each labor line row shows its own ⋮ menu on hover
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with two or more labor lines is open on the Lines tab.
column6:
1. Hover the first labor line row.
2. Hover the second labor line row.
column7:
1. Each labor line row shows its own ⋮ (more) button on hover.
2. Each menu has an 'Add Fee/Discount' item for that specific line.

column1: Verify a labor-line flat amount is the exact amount with no quantity multiplier
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line (any quantity/hours) is open.
column6:
1. Open the labor line's ⋮ menu and click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Set Type 'Fee', Calculation Type 'Flat Amount', '$ Amount' 50.
3. Save.
column7:
1. The result is exactly +$50.00 regardless of hours/quantity.
2. There is no Max Amount field for a flat amount.

column1: Verify a labor-line fee/discount works out to $0.00 when its line is not billable (declined)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line that carries a 10% fee adjustment resolving to a non-zero amount.
column6:
1. Set the labor line to Declined (not billable).
2. Look at the labor-line fee/discount's amount.
3. Make the line billable again.
4. Look at the amount again.
column7:
1. While the line is declined, the fee/discount works out to $0.00 but still shows.
2. Once the line is billable again, it works out to its non-zero amount.

column1: Verify deleting a labor line removes any fee/discount pointing to it
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a labor line that carries at least one fee/discount adjustment.
column6:
1. Delete the labor line (via its ⋮ / delete action).
2. Check the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card, the Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count, and the Stats breakdown.
column7:
1. The labor line is removed.
2. Any fee/discount that pointed to that line is also removed.
3. The Financial Info count and the Stats/Financial totals drop by the removed amount(s).

column1: Verify the labor-line 'Add Fee/Discount' is hidden without Work Order Lines: Create & Edit
column5:
1. Logged in as a role with See Financial Data but WITHOUT Work Order Lines: Create & Edit.
2. An open work order with a labor line is open.
column6:
1. As a role without Work Order Lines: Create & Edit, hover the labor line and open its ⋮ menu.
2. Look for 'Add Fee/Discount' and for Edit/Remove on any existing line fee/discount.
column7:
1. 'Add Fee/Discount' is not shown for the labor line.
2. Existing line fee/discount amounts are still visible (See Financial Data on) but have no Edit/Remove controls.

column1: Verify a part's ⋮ menu opens the Add Fee/Discount dialog locked to that part
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part, e.g. '(LF3620) Engine Oil Filter', is open on the Lines or Parts tab.
column6:
1. Hover the part row to show its ⋮ menu.
2. Click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
3. Read the dialog subtitle and the Calculation Type options.
column7:
1. The dialog 'Add new fee/discount' opens, locked to that part.
2. A grey subtitle reads 'Applying to: <part name>' (just the part name).
3. The Calculation Type options are 'Flat Amount' and '% of Parts Total' only.

column1: Verify a part-line flat amount is charged per item (amount x quantity): $5.00 x 3 → −$15.00
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part of quantity 3.
column6:
1. Open the part's ⋮ menu and click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Set Type 'Discount', Calculation Type 'Flat Amount', '$ Amount' 5.
3. Save.
4. Read the amount on the inline part row.
column7:
1. The discount is −$15.00 ($5.00 per item x quantity 3).
2. The inline part row shows the name with a −$5.00 flat rate badge and a resolved amount of −$15.00.
3. For a part-line flat amount, the amount is per item.

column1: Verify a fee/discount can be added to a requested (not-yet-received) part and shows before it is picked
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a requested (pending / not yet picked) part of quantity 2 at sell price $20.00 each.
column6:
1. Open the requested part's ⋮ menu and click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Set Type 'Discount', Calculation Type '% of Parts Total', 'Percent %' 10.
3. Save.
4. Look at the fee/discount on the requested part before it is picked.
column7:
1. The requested part's menu offers 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. The fee/discount shows on the requested part before it is picked.
3. It works out against quantity x sell price (for example 2 x $20.00 = $40.00 → 10% = −$4.00).

column1: Verify a part-line '% of Parts Total' works out against quantity x sell price
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part of quantity 3 at sell price $20.00 each (gross part total $60.00).
column6:
1. Open the part's ⋮ menu and click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Set Type 'Discount', Calculation Type '% of Parts Total', 'Percent %' 10.
3. Read the preview, then save.
column7:
1. The base is quantity x sell price = 3 x $20.00 = $60.00.
2. 10% of $60.00 = −$6.00.
3. The preview shows the part total and the new part total.

column1: Verify a part-line fee/discount stays attached when the part changes from requested to received
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a requested part that already carries a % of Parts Total discount.
column6:
1. Pick / receive the requested part so it becomes a received part.
2. Look at the fee/discount on the now-received part.
column7:
1. The fee/discount stays attached to the part after it goes from requested to received.
2. It keeps working out against quantity x sell price.
3. A received part cannot be pointed back to a request.

column1: Verify a part-line fee/discount works out to $0.00 when the part is declined or returned with no quantity left
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part carrying a discount that resolves to a non-zero amount.
column6:
1. Decline the part (or return it so no quantity is left).
2. Look at the fee/discount's amount.
3. Make the part billable again.
4. Look at the amount again.
column7:
1. While the part is not billable, the fee/discount works out to $0.00 but stays visible.
2. When the part is billable again (authorized, not declined, quantity left) it works out to its non-zero amount.

column1: Verify deleting a part removes any fee/discount pointing to it
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part that carries at least one adjustment.
column6:
1. Delete the part from the work order.
2. Check the Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count and the Stats breakdown.
column7:
1. The part is removed.
2. Any fee/discount pointing to that part is also removed.
3. The 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count and totals go down accordingly.

column1: Verify the per-item flat amount edge: quantity 1 is the base amount (−$5.00)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part of quantity 1.
column6:
1. Open the part's ⋮ menu and add a flat-amount discount of $5.00.
2. Save and read the amount.
3. Change the part quantity from 1 to 4 and re-check the amount.
column7:
1. At quantity 1 the discount is −$5.00 ($5.00 x 1).
2. After the quantity changes to 4 it re-works to −$20.00 ($5.00 x 4).

column1: Verify a labor-line fee/discount shows inline under its line with a ↳ arrow, name, signed rate and grey amount
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where a labor line has a fee/discount (for example a 'Line discount' of −5%).
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and find the labor line.
2. Read the 'Fees/Discounts' row shown indented under the line.
column7:
1. The fee/discount shows indented under the labor line with a '↳' arrow, on a row labelled 'Fees/Discounts'.
2. It shows the name and a signed rate badge (for example '−5%').
3. The resolved amount shows on the right in grey, signed (for example −$26.08).

column1: Verify a part-line fee/discount shows inline under its part with a ↳ arrow, name, signed rate and grey amount
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where a part has a fee/discount (for example a 'Parts Handling Fee' of +$3.75).
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and find the part row.
2. Read the 'Fees/Discounts' row shown indented under the part.
column7:
1. The fee/discount shows indented under the part with a '↳' arrow.
2. It shows the name and a signed rate badge (a dollar amount for a flat amount, or a percentage).
3. The resolved amount shows on the right in grey, signed (for example +$3.75).

column1: Verify a line/part with 2 or more fees/discounts shows only the first plus a 'Show N more' toggle
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where one part has three fees/discounts.
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and find the part with three fees/discounts.
2. See how many fee/discount rows show by default.
3. Click 'Show 2 more'.
4. Read the toggle label after it expands.
column7:
1. By default only the first fee/discount row shows.
2. A 'Show 2 more' toggle is shown (the number is how many are hidden).
3. Clicking it shows the other two rows.
4. The toggle then reads 'Show less'.

column1: Verify the per-line Total column shows the line's own total plus its fee/discount amounts (display only)
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where a part has a base total plus a few fees/discounts.
column6:
1. Go to the Lines tab and find the part.
2. Read the part's Total column, which stacks the base total and each fee/discount amount.
3. Check whether any stored prices change.
column7:
1. The Total column stacks the base total and each fee/discount row, so the shown total matches the rows.
2. This is display only and changes no stored value.

column1: Verify each inline fee/discount row has a ⋮ menu with Edit and Remove (when the work order is open and you have the matching Create and Edit permission)
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with at least one inline line-level fee/discount.
column6:
1. Hover an inline fee/discount row.
2. Open its ⋮ (more) menu.
column7:
1. A ⋮ menu appears on the row.
2. The menu offers 'Edit' and 'Remove'.
3. The menu shows only when the work order is open and you have the matching Create and Edit permission.

column1: Verify the Stats tab shows a 'Fees & Discounts (N)' breakdown with a value/% and an amount for each row
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with several fees/discounts across scopes is open.
column6:
1. Open the work order's Stats tab.
2. Find the 'Fees & Discounts (N)' section (below the Hours, Labor, Parts and Total sections).
3. Read each row.
column7:
1. A 'Fees & Discounts (N)' section is shown, where N is the total number of fees/discounts of any scope.
2. Each row shows the name, a value/percentage for percentage fees/discounts (for example '−50%'), and the signed resolved amount on the right.

column1: Verify each Stats fee/discount row names its target
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a whole-work-order discount and line-level part/labor fees/discounts.
column6:
1. Open the Stats tab and find the 'Fees & Discounts' section.
2. Read what each row shows to identify its target.
3. Try clicking a line-level row's target.
column7:
1. A whole-work-order fee/discount shows the work order it belongs to.
2. A line-level fee/discount names the line/part it belongs to.
3. The target is a link you can click to jump to that line/part.

column1: Verify the Stats 'Fees & Discounts' total equals the signed sum of all the amounts
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a mix of fees and discounts.
column6:
1. Open the Stats tab 'Fees & Discounts' section.
2. Check the sign shown for a fee vs a discount vs a flat amount.
3. Read the total of the section.
column7:
1. A fee shows a '+' and a discount shows a '−'; a flat amount shows no percentage.
2. The total equals the signed sum of every resolved amount (for example −857.23 − 649.00 − 292.00 + 3.75 − 260.77 = −$2,055.25).

column1: Verify the Stats fees/discounts are listed in the order they were created (oldest first)
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where you add three fees/discounts in a known order: A first, B second, C third.
column6:
1. Add A, then B, then C.
2. Open the Stats tab 'Fees & Discounts' section.
3. Read the top-to-bottom order of the rows.
column7: 1. The rows are listed oldest first: A, then B, then C.

column1: Verify the Stats 'Fees & Discounts' section is hidden when the work order has no fees/discounts
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with no fees/discounts of any scope.
column6:
1. Open the Stats tab.
2. Look for a 'Fees & Discounts' section.
column7: 1. There is no 'Fees & Discounts' section when the work order has no fees/discounts.

column1: Verify the Financial Info card shows a 'Fees & Discounts (N)' row with the net total in grey
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order that has several fees/discounts (any scope) is open.
column6:
1. Look at the 'Financial Info' card on the left.
2. Find the 'Fees & Discounts (N)' row.
3. Read the count and the net total shown on that row.
column7:
1. A 'Fees & Discounts (N)' row is shown, where N is the total number of fees/discounts of any scope on the work order.
2. The row shows the net total of all fees/discounts in grey (for example a net of −$2,055.25 across 5 fees/discounts).
3. The row sits with the other money rows (Parts, Labor, Shop Supplies, Subtotal, GST, Total, Balance).

column1: Verify the Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts' row lists each fee/discount and is read-only
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with several fees/discounts of mixed scope is open.
column6:
1. Open (expand) the 'Fees & Discounts (N)' row in the Financial Info card.
2. Read the fees/discounts and their amounts.
3. Look for any add, edit or remove buttons in this card.
column7:
1. Each fee/discount is listed in the order it was created (oldest first), with its name and its amount in grey.
2. This card is read-only — there is no add, edit or remove control anywhere in it.

column1: Verify the 'Fees & Discounts' row is hidden with no fees/discounts, and the money section is hidden without See Financial Data
column5:
1. Case (a): logged in with See Financial Data, an open work order with no fees/discounts.
2. Case (b): logged in as a role WITHOUT See Financial Data, an open work order that has fees/discounts.
column6:
1. Case (a): open the work order and check the Financial Info card for a 'Fees & Discounts (N)' row.
2. Case (b): open the work order and look at the Financial Info money section.
column7:
1. Case (a): with no fees/discounts of any scope, there is no 'Fees & Discounts (N)' row.
2. Case (b): without See Financial Data, the Financial Info money section (and all fee/discount amounts) is hidden.

column1: Verify the sidebar 'WO Fees & Discounts' card lists whole-work-order fees/discounts with name, signed rate and grey amount
column2: Work Order — Sidebar 'Work Order Fee / Discount' card
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data and Work Orders: Create & Edit.
2. An open work order with a whole-work-order discount plus some line-level fees/discounts.
column6:
1. Look at the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card on the left.
2. Read the listed entries and check which scopes appear.
3. Open an entry's ⋮ (more) menu.
column7:
1. The card is titled 'WO Fees & Discounts' and lists ONLY whole-work-order fees/discounts — line-level ones do not appear here.
2. Each entry shows its name, a signed rate badge (for example '−8%' or a dollar amount) and the resolved amount in grey, signed.
3. The entry's ⋮ menu offers 'Edit' and 'Remove'.

column1: Verify the sidebar 'WO Fees & Discounts' card is hidden with no whole-work-order fees/discounts and has no Add button
column2: Work Order — Sidebar 'Work Order Fee / Discount' card
column5:
1. You are logged in with See Financial Data and Work Orders: Create & Edit.
2. Case (a): an open work order with only line-level fees/discounts and no whole-work-order ones.
3. Case (b): an open work order with at least one whole-work-order fee/discount.
column6:
1. Case (a): open the work order and look for the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card.
2. Case (b): open the work order, view the card, and look for any 'Add' button inside it.
column7:
1. Case (a): the card is hidden when there are no whole-work-order fees/discounts.
2. Case (b): the card has no 'Add' button — you add fees/discounts only from the work order ⋯ menu and the line/part menus.

column1: Verify the Parts page 'Fees & Discounts' column shows a single fee/discount's name and rate
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. A Parts page / WO parts view is open with part '#37346 Mobil 1 5W20' carrying exactly one adjustment 'Military Discount' −10%.
column6:
1. Find a part in the parts table that has one fee/discount.
2. Read its 'Fees & Discounts' column cell.
column7:
1. The cell shows the fee/discount's name and rate (for example 'Military Discount −10%').
2. Clicking the cell opens the breakdown view.

column1: Verify the 'Fees & Discounts' column shows a '+N' badge when a part has several fees/discounts
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. Parts page open with part '#55073 Mobil 1 5W20' carrying three adjustments (first = 'Parts Handling Fee' 2%).
column6:
1. Find a part that has more than one fee/discount.
2. Read its 'Fees & Discounts' column cell.
column7: 1. The cell shows the first fee/discount followed by a '+N' badge (N = how many more there are).

column1: Verify the 'Fees & Discounts' column shows a '+ Add' button on a part with no fees/discounts
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data and the matching Create and Edit permission.
2. Parts page open with part '#28439 Fleetguard FF5421' carrying no adjustments, on an editable sale/WO.
column6:
1. Find a part with no fees/discounts.
2. Read its 'Fees & Discounts' column cell.
3. Click the '+ Add' button.
column7:
1. The cell shows a '+ Add' button.
2. Clicking it opens the Add fee/discount dialog locked to that part.

column1: Verify clicking a filled 'Fees & Discounts' cell opens the per-part breakdown with the right columns
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. Parts page open with part '#55073 Mobil 1 5W20' carrying three adjustments (Parts Handling Fee +$1.43, Military Discount −$3.31, Early Payment Discount −$0.99).
column6:
1. Click a part's filled 'Fees & Discounts' cell.
2. Read the title and column headers.
3. Read each row.
column7:
1. A 'Fees & Discounts' view opens, named for the part.
2. The columns are Name, Type, Calculation, Amount, Max Amount, and a remove control.
3. Each row shows the calculation phrasing and a signed amount.
4. There is a 'Close' button.

column1: Verify the breakdown 'Net adjustment' row equals the signed sum of the part's fees/discounts
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. The #55073 breakdown modal is open (Parts Handling Fee +$1.43, Military Discount −$3.31, Early Payment Discount −$0.99).
column6: 1. Read the 'Net adjustment' row at the bottom of the breakdown.
column7: 1. 'Net adjustment' shows the signed sum of all the part's fees/discounts.

column1: Verify a per-row Remove on the breakdown removes the fee/discount and closes when the last one is removed
column5:
1. Logged in with the matching Create and Edit permission + See Financial Data.
2. Parts page open with part #37346 carrying exactly ONE adjustment; the editable breakdown modal is open.
column6:
1. Confirm each row has a remove (trash) control.
2. Click remove on the only fee/discount.
3. Look at the view and the part's 'Fees & Discounts' cell afterwards.
column7:
1. The fee/discount is removed.
2. Because it was the last one, the view closes on its own.
3. The part's cell goes back to the '+ Add' empty state.

column1: Verify the '+ Add' button is disabled when the sale/work order cannot be edited
column5:
1. Logged in with See Financial Data.
2. Parts page open for an Invoiced/Paid (non-editable) sale/WO with a part that has no adjustments.
column6:
1. Find a part with no fees/discounts on a sale/work order that cannot be edited.
2. Look at its '+ Add' button.
column7:
1. The '+ Add' button is disabled because the sale/work order cannot be edited.
2. Filled cells still open a read-only breakdown, but the per-row remove controls are not shown.

column1: Verify editing a fee/discount allows Name, amount, Max Amount and Taxable but locks Type, Calculation Type and Scope
column5:
1. You are logged in with the matching Create and Edit permission and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with an existing whole-work-order percentage discount.
column6:
1. On the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card, open the entry's ⋮ menu and click 'Edit'.
2. Check which fields you can change and which are greyed out.
3. Change the Name and the Percent value, then click 'Save'.
column7:
1. The dialog title reads 'Edit Fee / Discount'.
2. Name, the amount (or Percent), Max Amount and the Taxable toggle can be changed.
3. Type and Calculation Type are shown but greyed out and cannot be changed.
4. The scope (whole work order) cannot be changed.
5. The change saves and a success message confirms it.

column1: Verify editing re-works the amount against the current totals, hides the template picker, and uses a 'Save' button
column5:
1. You are logged in with the matching Create and Edit permission and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with an existing percentage fee/discount whose base total has since changed (for example a line was added).
column6:
1. Open the fee/discount's Edit dialog.
2. Check that there is no 'Apply From Template' dropdown.
3. Change the Percent value and click 'Save'.
4. Read the resolved amount and the tax after saving.
column7:
1. There is no 'Apply From Template' dropdown in the Edit dialog.
2. The confirm button reads 'Save'.
3. When you save, the fee/discount is worked out again against the work order's current totals.
4. Both the resolved amount and the tax update.

column1: Verify a failed save keeps the Edit dialog open and shows the error
column5:
1. You are logged in with the matching Create and Edit permission and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with an existing fee/discount, and a way to make the save fail (for example a server error).
column6:
1. Open the fee/discount's Edit dialog and change a field.
2. Save in a way the server rejects.
3. Look at the dialog and any error message.
column7:
1. The dialog stays open.
2. An error message tells you the save did not work.

column1: Verify removing a whole-work-order fee/discount shows the 'Remove Fee / Discount' confirm and a success message
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a whole-work-order fee/discount.
column6:
1. On the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card, open the entry's ⋮ menu.
2. Click 'Remove'.
3. Read the confirm dialog.
4. Click the 'Remove' button in the dialog.
column7:
1. A confirm dialog opens titled 'Remove Fee / Discount' with the message 'Are you sure you want to remove this fee?' and a 'Remove' button (and a 'Cancel' button).
2. After you confirm, the fee/discount is removed.
3. A success message confirms it, and the entry disappears from the card while the count and totals update.

column1: Verify removing a fee/discount uses Create and Edit, not a separate Delete permission
column5:
1. You are logged in as a role that HAS Work Orders: Create & Edit and See Financial Data but does NOT have a separate 'Delete' permission.
2. An open work order with a whole-work-order fee/discount.
column6:
1. Open the entry's ⋮ menu on the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card.
2. Check that a 'Remove' option is present and works.
3. Remove the fee/discount.
column7:
1. The 'Remove' option is available and works even though you do not have a separate Delete permission.
2. The fee/discount is removed.
3. By contrast, a user without Create & Edit sees no 'Remove' option and cannot remove it.

column1: Verify removing a line-level fee/discount from its inline ⋮ menu
column5:
1. You are logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order where a part has a fee/discount shown inline.
column6:
1. Hover the inline fee/discount row on the part.
2. Open its ⋮ menu and click 'Remove'.
3. Confirm in the 'Remove Fee / Discount' dialog.
4. Look at the inline rows and the part Total column.
column7:
1. The 'Remove Fee / Discount' confirm appears; after you confirm, the fee/discount is removed.
2. The inline row disappears and the part Total column updates.
3. A success message confirms the removal.

column1: Verify multiple fees/discounts on one part each work out on the part's own total (they do not compound)
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Order Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with a part of gross part total exactly $100.00.
column6:
1. Add a part-line discount: '% of Parts Total' 10%.
2. Add a second part-line discount: '% of Parts Total' 5%.
3. Add a part-line fee: 'Flat Amount' $2.00 (part quantity 1).
4. Read each amount on the part's inline rows and the net.
column7:
1. The 10% discount works out on the part's total $100.00 → −$10.00 (not on the already-discounted amount — line-level fees/discounts do not compound).
2. The 5% discount also works out on $100.00 → −$5.00.
3. The flat fee is +$2.00 ($2.00 x quantity 1).
4. The net is −10.00 − 5.00 + 2.00 = −$13.00.

column1: Verify two whole-work-order percentage fees/discounts use the same totals and do not change each other's base
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit, Work Order Lines: Create & Edit, and See Financial Data.
2. An open work order with Gross Labor $200.00 and Gross Parts $100.00, no shop supplies.
3. A Labor Line 10% discount already applied (Step 1: −$20.00, so Net Labor = $180.00).
column6:
1. Add a labor-line discount '% of Labor Total' 10% on the $200 labor line.
2. Add a whole-work-order fee '% of Labor Total' 5%.
3. Add a whole-work-order discount '% of Parts Total' 10%.
4. Read each amount.
column7:
1. The labor-line discount works out first: 10% x $200.00 = −$20.00, so net labor is $180.00.
2. The whole-work-order 5% fee (% of Labor Total) = 5% x $180.00 = +$9.00 (uses the net labor).
3. The whole-work-order 10% discount (% of Parts Total) = 10% x $100.00 = −$10.00.
4. The two whole-work-order ones do not change each other's base.

column1: Verify the same template can be applied to one work order more than once by hand
column5:
1. Logged in with Work Orders: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
2. An open work order; the location library has a 'Parts Handling Fee' template.
column6:
1. Open 'Add Fee/Discount' from the ⋯ menu, pick a template in 'Apply From Template', and Save.
2. Repeat: open the dialog again, pick the same template, and Save.
3. Look at the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card and the Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts (N)' count.
column7:
1. Both are added; the same template appears twice as two independent fees/discounts.
2. The count and totals reflect both.
column8: Overview 'apply same template more than once' / §3 key decisions

column1: Verify the Part Sale Add/Edit fee-or-discount dialog shows the tax-jurisdiction note below the Taxable toggle
column5:
You are signed in as a user with Part Sales: Create and Edit plus See Financial Data.
You are on an editable Part Sale (for example an Approved part sale).
column6:
1. From the Part Sale toolbar ⋮ menu choose 'Add Parts Sale Fee / Discount' (whole sale), or from a part row's ⋮ menu choose 'Add Fee / Discount' (part line).
2. In the 'Add new fee/discount' dialog look directly below the 'Taxable' Yes/No toggle for a note.
3. Open an existing part-sale fee/discount's Edit dialog and check the same place.
column7:
1. Directly below the Taxable toggle this note is shown: 'Tax treatment varies by jurisdiction — confirm your local requirements before saving.'
2. The same note shows for both the whole-sale dialog and the per-part dialog (the per-part dialog also shows an 'Applying to: Part — (part number) name' subtitle).
3. The same note shows in both the Add and the Edit dialog.
4. The note is shown only to users with See Financial Data.

column1: Verify the customer 'Fees & Discounts (N)' tab shows the correct default count
column5:
1. A test customer named ZZAUTOTEST Customer exists with exactly 2 default fees/discounts linked.
2. You are logged in with Customer Management: Create & Edit and Manage AP/AR permissions.
column6:
1. Go to Customers and open a customer record.
2. Look at the row of tabs (Work Orders, Part Sales, Contacts, Assets, Notes, Invoices, Payments, Deposits, Fees & Discounts).
3. Read the label on the Fees & Discounts tab.
column7:
1. A tab labelled 'Fees & Discounts (N)' is shown, where N is the number of defaults linked to this customer.
2. A customer with no defaults shows 'Fees & Discounts (0)'.

column1: Verify the 'Default Fees & Discounts' card header, caption and table columns
column5:
1. A customer with at least 1 default fee/discount exists.
2. You have Customer Management: Create & Edit + Manage AP/AR.
column6:
1. Open a customer and click the 'Fees & Discounts (N)' tab.
2. Read the card title, the caption, the 'Add Fee/Discount' button and the table column headers.
column7:
1. The card title reads 'Default Fees & Discounts'.
2. There is an 'Add Fee/Discount' button in the card.
3. The caption reads: 'These fees & discounts auto-apply to every new work order for this customer. They can still be edited or removed on individual work orders without changing the defaults here.'
4. The table columns, left to right, are: Name, Type, Calculation Type, Amount, Max Amount, Taxable, plus a remove action.

column1: Verify adding a single template as a customer default via the picker
column5:
1. A location template named "ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Discount" (Discount, % of Subtotal, 10%) exists and is NOT yet linked to the test customer.
2. You have Customer Management: Create & Edit + Manage AP/AR.
column6:
1. Open the customer, go to the Fees & Discounts tab, click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. In the 'Fee / Discount Templates' dropdown, pick one template.
3. Click 'Save'.
column7:
1. The picker is a single-select dropdown of available templates — one is picked and added at a time.
2. After Save the picker closes and a success message appears.
3. The picked template now appears as a row in the Default Fees & Discounts table and the tab count goes up by 1.
4. The new default's columns match the template (Type, Calculation Type, Amount).

column1: Verify several templates are added as customer defaults one at a time (no multi-select)
column5:
1. At least 3 templates exist that are NOT yet linked to the test customer.
2. You have Customer Management: Create & Edit + Manage AP/AR.
column6:
1. Open the customer, Fees & Discounts tab, click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Pick the first template and click 'Save'.
3. Repeat for the second and third templates, one at a time.
column7:
1. The picker lets you add only one template per add — there is no way to tick several at once.
2. Each add closes the picker and shows its own success message.
3. After the three adds, all 3 templates appear in the table and the tab count goes up by 3.

column1: Verify the picker lists only not-yet-added templates and shows a Processing Fee template as type 'Fee'
column5:
1. The location has: (a) a template already linked to this customer, (b) an unlinked Fee/Discount template, and (c) an unlinked Processing Fee template.
2. You have Customer Management: Create & Edit + Manage AP/AR.
column6:
1. Open the customer, Fees & Discounts tab, click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
2. Open the 'Fee / Discount Templates' dropdown and review the templates offered.
column7:
1. The picker is a single-select dropdown.
2. A template already added as a default does not appear in the picker.
3. A not-yet-added Fee/Discount template appears.
4. A Processing Fee template also appears (it can be a customer default), and in the current build its Type shows as 'Fee'.
column8: S9-R19, S8-R15, S9-R... (Processing Fee shows as "Fee")

column1: Verify the picker message when there are no templates left to add
column5: 1. Every location template is already linked to the test customer (or the location has no templates).
column6:
1. Add every template as a default so none are left.
2. Open the customer, Fees & Discounts tab, click 'Add Fee/Discount'.
3. Open the 'Fee / Discount Templates' dropdown.
column7: 1. The dropdown shows a 'No results' empty state and offers no templates to add.

column1: Verify removing a customer default from the row needs no confirmation
column5: 1. The customer has at least 1 default fee/discount.
column6:
1. Open the customer, Fees & Discounts tab.
2. On a default row, find the remove (trash) action.
3. Click the remove (trash) icon.
column7:
1. Each row has only a remove (trash) action (no inline Edit, no separate Delete).
2. No confirmation dialog appears; the default is removed straight away.
3. A success message appears.
4. The row disappears and the tab count goes down by 1.

column1: Verify the empty-state text on the Default Fees & Discounts card
column5: 1. The customer has zero default fees/discounts.
column6:
1. Open a customer with no defaults, Fees & Discounts tab.
2. Read the card body.
column7:
1. The card shows "No fees or discounts yet. Use 'Add Fee/Discount' to add one."
2. The tab reads 'Fees & Discounts (0)'.

column1: Verify a customer default is added as its own fee/discount on every new work order
column5: 1. The customer has a default "ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Discount" (Discount, % of Subtotal, 10%, non-taxable).
column6:
1. Create a new work order for this customer with at least one labor line and one part so the subtotal is not zero.
2. Open the work order's 'WO Fees & Discounts' card and the Financial Info 'Fees & Discounts (N)' row.
3. Edit the fee/discount on the work order (change its name), then re-open the customer's Fees & Discounts tab.
column7:
1. The new work order automatically carries a whole-work-order fee/discount copied from the default (name, type, method, amount, taxable, Max Amount as they were at creation).
2. It works out against the work order's net subtotal.
3. Editing it on the work order does not change the customer's default.

column1: Verify a percentage customer default re-works per work order (keeps the percent, not a fixed dollar)
column5: 1. The customer has a default "ZZAUTOTEST 10% Fee" (Fee, % of Subtotal, 10%, taxable).
column6:
1. Create work order #1 for this customer with a net subtotal of $150.00; note the fee amount.
2. Create work order #2 for the same customer with a net subtotal of $300.00; note the fee amount.
column7:
1. Work order #1 shows the fee at +$15.00 (10% of $150.00).
2. Work order #2 shows the fee at +$30.00 (10% of $300.00).
3. The default stores the 10% rate, not a fixed dollar amount, so the dollar value differs per work order.

column1: Verify removing a customer default does not change fees/discounts already on existing work orders
column5:
1. The customer has a default "ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Discount".
2. An OPEN work order for that customer already carries the auto-added adjustment from this default.
column6:
1. Open the customer's Fees & Discounts tab and remove a default.
2. Open a work order that already has that fee/discount and check its 'WO Fees & Discounts' card and Financial Info row.
column7:
1. The default is removed from the customer.
2. The existing work order still shows its fee/discount unchanged.
3. Only new work orders created after the removal will lack it.

column1: Verify deleting a template that is a customer default drops the default link but keeps existing work-order fees/discounts
column5: 1. A template "ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Discount" is a default on the customer AND has been auto-added to an existing OPEN work order.
column6:
1. Go to Administration → Finance → Fees & Discounts and delete a template that is a customer default (confirm).
2. Open the customer's Fees & Discounts tab.
3. Open a work order that already has a fee/discount made from that template.
column7:
1. The template is deleted from the library.
2. The customer's default link to it is removed (the tab count goes down).
3. The existing work order's fee/discount stays unchanged.

column1: Verify deleting a customer removes that customer's default links
column5: 1. A disposable ZZAUTOTEST customer has at least 1 default fee/discount linked.
column6:
1. Delete a ZZAUTOTEST customer.
2. Confirm the templates that were its defaults still exist in Administration → Finance → Fees & Discounts.
column7:
1. The customer and its default links are removed.
2. The location templates are not deleted (only the customer's links go away).

column1: Verify a brand-new customer inherits every auto-apply location template as a default
column5: 1. The location has exactly 2 templates marked auto-apply and 1 template not auto-apply.
column6:
1. Create a brand-new customer at this location.
2. Open the new customer's Fees & Discounts tab.
column7:
1. Every auto-apply template is already present as a default (the tab count matches the number of auto-apply templates).
2. Templates that are not auto-apply are not added.

column1: Verify the customer Fees & Discounts tab and its controls are hidden without the required permissions
column5: 1. A ZZAUTOTEST role is assigned to Tech (exact-user-match) with Customer Management: Create & Edit ON but Manage Accounts Payable and Receivable OFF.
column6:
1. Log in as a role without Manage AP/AR (for example Tech) and open a customer record.
2. Look for the Fees & Discounts tab and the 'Add Fee/Discount' button.
3. Restore the role afterward.
column7:
1. Without Manage AP/AR, the customer 'Fees & Discounts' tab and its controls are hidden.
2. Both Customer Management: Create & Edit AND Manage AP/AR are needed to view/change customer defaults; missing either hides the tab and controls.

column1: Verify an add/remove/load failure on customer defaults shows the standard error notification
column2: API — Customer Fees & Discounts tab — negative
column5: 1. A way to force a server error (e.g., simulate a network/API failure) on the add or remove call.
column6:
1. On the customer Fees & Discounts tab, trigger an add or remove while the back-end call fails.
2. Look at the feedback.
column7:
1. The system shows its standard error notification (no custom per-action wording).
2. The default list is not left half-changed (the failed action is not partly applied).

column1: Verify the fee/discount template library is at Administration → Finance → Fees & Discounts (below Payment Methods)
column5: 1. You have Settings → Finance access.
column6:
1. Open Administration (the gear/admin area).
2. In the left menu, look under the 'FINANCE' heading.
3. Click 'Fees & Discounts'.
column7:
1. A 'Fees & Discounts' page opens.
2. In the left menu it sits under 'FINANCE', directly below 'Payment Methods'.

column1: Verify the template list columns and the edit/delete actions
column5: 1. The location has at least 1 template.
column6:
1. Open Administration → Finance → Fees & Discounts.
2. Read the table column headers and the row buttons.
column7:
1. The columns, left to right, are: Name, Type, Calculation Type, Amount, Max Amount, Taxable, Auto-Apply To Work Orders.
2. Each row has an edit (pencil) button and a delete (red trash) button.

column1: Verify creating a Fee template (dialog fields and the Create button)
column5: 1. You are on Administration → Service → Fees & Discounts.
column6:
1. Click 'New Fee / Discount'.
2. Check the dialog title reads 'New Fee / Discount'.
3. Set Type to 'Fee'; Calculation Type to '% of Labor Total'; Name 'ZZAUTOTEST Shop Fee'; Percent 5; leave Max Amount blank; leave the Taxable toggle on; optionally add a Description; leave 'Auto-apply to new work orders' off.
4. Click 'Create'.
column7:
1. The dialog has: Name, Type (Fee or Discount), Calculation Type, '$ Default Amount' (or Percent for a percentage method), 'Max Amount (Optional)' (percentage methods only), a Taxable toggle (on by default), an 'Auto-apply to new work orders' toggle, and a 'Description (Optional)' field.
2. There is no scope field (every template is whole-work-order).
3. The confirm button reads 'Create'.
4. On save a success message appears and the new template appears in the list.

column1: Verify creating a Discount template
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts page.
column6:
1. Click 'New Fee / Discount'.
2. Set Type 'Discount'; Calculation Type '% of Subtotal'; Name 'ZZAUTOTEST Loyalty'; Percent 8; turn the Taxable toggle off.
3. Click 'Create'.
column7:
1. The save succeeds and a success message appears (a generic message, not a per-type 'Discount added').
2. The list shows 'ZZAUTOTEST Loyalty', Type Discount, Calculation Type % of Subtotal, Amount −8%, Taxable No.

column1: Verify the 'Auto-apply to new work orders' toggle adds the template to every new work order at that location
column5: 1. You can create a template and then a new work order at the same location.
column6:
1. Create a template 'ZZAUTOTEST Auto Fee' (Fee, Flat Amount, $10.00, taxable) with the 'Auto-apply to new work orders' toggle turned on.
2. Create a new work order at that location.
3. Open the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card on the work order.
column7:
1. The toggle in the template dialog is labelled 'Auto-apply to new work orders'.
2. The new work order automatically has a whole-work-order fee 'ZZAUTOTEST Auto Fee' = +$10.00.
3. The added fee copies the template's name, type, method, amount, taxable and Max Amount as they were when the work order was created.

column1: Verify editing a template (Edit Fee / Discount dialog, 'Save' button)
column5: 1. A Fee template "ZZAUTOTEST Shop Fee" exists.
column6:
1. On the Fees & Discounts admin page, click the pencil (edit) button on the 'ZZAUTOTEST Shop Fee' row.
2. Check the dialog title reads 'Edit Fee / Discount'.
3. Change the Percent from 5 to 7 and click 'Save'.
column7:
1. The Edit dialog is titled 'Edit Fee / Discount'.
2. The confirm button reads 'Save'; Type and Calculation Type are locked.
3. On save a success message appears and the list shows the new 7% value.

column1: Verify the template delete confirm dialog and buttons
column5: 1. A template that is NOT a default for any customer exists.
column6:
1. On the Fees & Discounts admin page, click the delete (trash) button on a template.
2. Read the confirm dialog.
column7:
1. A confirm dialog titled 'Delete Template' opens.
2. It has a 'Cancel' button and a red 'Delete' button.
3. Confirming removes the template from the list.

column1: Verify the delete confirm adds a warning when the template is a customer default
column5: 1. A template is set as a default for exactly 2 customers.
column6:
1. On the Fees & Discounts admin page, click the delete (trash) button on a template that is set as a default for one or more customers.
2. Read the confirm dialog.
column7:
1. The 'Delete Template' confirm dialog opens.
2. It shows the warning 'This template is set as a default for N customer(s). Deleting it will remove it from them.' — N is how many customers currently have it as a default.

column1: Verify deleting a template leaves work-order fees/discounts made from it unchanged
column5: 1. A template has been applied to an OPEN work order as an adjustment.
column6:
1. Delete the template from Administration → Finance → Fees & Discounts (confirm).
2. Open a work order that already has a fee/discount made from that template and check the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card.
column7:
1. The template is removed from the library.
2. The work order's fee/discount made from it stays unchanged (same name, amount, taxable).

column1: Verify template scoping — labour-method templates only show in labour pickers, parts-method only in parts pickers
column5:
1. The location has: a "% of Labor Total" template, a "% of Parts Total" template, and a Flat Amount template.
2. A work order with at least one labor line and one part exists.
column6:
1. On a labor line's ⋮ menu, click 'Add Fee/Discount' and open the 'Apply From Template' picker.
2. Note which templates are offered.
3. Cancel; on a part's ⋮ menu click 'Add Fee/Discount' and open the same picker.
4. Note which templates are offered.
column7:
1. From a labor line, the picker lists only Flat Amount and '% of Labor Total' templates (not '% of Parts Total').
2. From a part, the picker lists only Flat Amount and '% of Parts Total' templates (not '% of Labor Total').
3. Neither picker lists a Processing Fee template.

column1: Verify Max Amount shows only for percentage methods and how 0 behaves
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6:
1. Set Calculation Type to 'Flat Amount' and check whether 'Max Amount (Optional)' shows.
2. Switch to '% of Subtotal' and check again.
3. Enter 0 into Max Amount and save.
column7:
1. For 'Flat Amount' there is no Max Amount field.
2. For a percentage method the 'Max Amount (Optional)' field shows.
3. A Max Amount of 0 is treated exactly the same as leaving it empty = no cap (working as designed per S2-R25).

column1: Verify the template list empty-state message
column5: 1. The location has zero templates.
column6:
1. Open Administration → Finance → Fees & Discounts on a location that has no templates.
2. Read the empty-state message.
column7: 1. The page shows an empty-state message inviting you to create your first fee/discount.

column1: Verify a percentage-discount template cannot go over 100% while a percentage-fee template has no cap
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6:
1. Set Type 'Discount', Calculation Type '% of Subtotal', Percent 150, and try to save.
2. Change Type to 'Fee', Percent 150, and try to save.
column7:
1. The 150% discount is rejected (a percentage discount cannot be more than 100%).
2. The 150% fee is accepted (percentage fees have no upper limit).

column1: Verify a Fee/Discount template offers the four whole-work-order methods and no scope field
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog with Type = Fee or Discount.
column6:
1. Open the Calculation Type dropdown in the template dialog.
2. Look for any scope field.
column7:
1. The Calculation Type options are: Flat Amount, % of Labor Total, % of Parts Total, % of Subtotal.
2. There is no Labor Line or Part Line method and no scope field (every template is whole-work-order).

column1: Verify the template save-failure message
column5: 1. A way to force a save failure on the template create/edit call.
column6:
1. Fill in a valid template and save while the save fails (for example a server error).
2. Look at the message.
column7: 1. An error message tells you the fee/discount could not be saved and to try again.

column1: Verify the admin Fees & Discounts page needs the Settings → Finance permission
column5: 1. A ZZAUTOTEST role is assigned to Tech (exact-user-match) WITHOUT Settings → Finance.
column6:
1. Log in as a role without Settings → Finance (for example Tech) and try to reach Administration → Finance → Fees & Discounts.
2. Restore the role afterward.
column7: 1. Without Settings → Finance, the admin Fees & Discounts page cannot be opened and templates cannot be created/edited/deleted.

column1: Verify the template Name is limited to 100 characters
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6:
1. Type a 100-character name and confirm it is accepted.
2. Try to type a 101st character.
column7:
1. Up to 100 characters are accepted.
2. The 101st character is not accepted.

column1: Verify 'Processing Fee' is a third Type in the template builder
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog.
column6: 1. Open the Type dropdown in the template create dialog.
column7:
1. The Type dropdown offers 'Fee', 'Discount' and 'Processing Fee'.
2. A Processing Fee can be created only here (as a template).

column1: Verify a Processing Fee offers only Flat Amount and % of Grand Total
column5: 1. On the admin Fees & Discounts create dialog with Type = "Processing Fee".
column6:
1. With Type set to 'Processing Fee', open the Calculation Type dropdown.
2. For comparison, switch Type back to 'Fee' and open the dropdown.
column7:
1. For a Processing Fee, Calculation Type offers only 'Flat Amount' (default) and '% of Grand Total'.
2. '% of Grand Total' is offered only for a Processing Fee.
3. '% of Grand Total' uses a base that includes tax (net subtotal + tax on it).

column1: Verify the Max Amount field is hidden for a Processing Fee (both methods)
column5: 1. On the admin create dialog with Type = Processing Fee.
column6:
1. With Type 'Processing Fee' and Calculation Type 'Flat Amount', check for a Max Amount field.
2. Switch to '% of Grand Total' and check again.
column7: 1. No Max Amount field is shown for a Processing Fee under either method.

column1: Verify the Processing Fee Taxable defaults to Yes and shows the tax-jurisdiction note
column5: 1. On the admin create dialog with Type = Processing Fee.
column6:
1. Look at the Taxable control's default value.
2. Read any note shown below the Taxable setting.
column7:
1. Taxable defaults to 'Yes'.
2. Directly below Taxable this note shows: 'Tax treatment varies by jurisdiction — confirm your local requirements before saving.'
3. The note is plain advice to the shop, not a system instruction or a legal statement.
4. The note is shown only to users with See Financial Data — a user without See Financial Data does not see the note.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee cannot be added to a work order by hand
column5:
1. A Processing Fee template exists.
2. An open work order is available.
column6:
1. On the work order ⋯ menu click 'Add Fee/Discount' and open the Type dropdown.
2. Open the 'Apply From Template' dropdown here and from a labor line and a part dialog.
column7:
1. The work order Add dialog Type dropdown does not list 'Processing Fee' (only Fee and Discount).
2. The 'Apply From Template' dropdown does not list any Processing Fee template from any starting place.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee reaches a new work order via location auto-apply
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template "ZZAUTOTEST Proc Fee" (Flat Amount $5.00, taxable Yes) is marked auto-apply.
column6:
1. Create a new work order at that location.
2. Open the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card.
column7:
1. The new work order carries a whole-work-order Processing Fee.
2. In its ⋮ menu, 'Remove' works but 'Edit' does nothing for a Processing Fee.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee reaches a new work order via a customer default
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template is set as a default on the test customer.
column6:
1. Create a new work order for that customer.
2. Open the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card.
column7:
1. The new work order carries the Processing Fee as its own whole-work-order fee (an independent copy).
2. In its ⋮ menu, 'Remove' works but 'Edit' does nothing for a Processing Fee.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee on a work order can be removed but not edited
column5: 1. An open WO carries a Processing Fee (via auto-apply or customer default).
column6:
1. Open the Processing Fee entry's ⋮ menu in the 'WO Fees & Discounts' card.
2. Note the options, then remove it.
column7:
1. The menu shows 'Edit' and 'Remove'; 'Edit' does nothing for a Processing Fee (it cannot be edited on the work order).
2. 'Remove' opens the 'Remove Fee / Discount' confirm and removes it on confirm.
3. To change the amount/method/taxable you edit the template, not the work-order copy.

column1: Verify a % of Grand Total Processing Fee works out last on the tax-included grand total (3% of $324 → +$9.72)
column5:
1. A Processing Fee template "ZZAUTOTEST 3% Proc" (% of Grand Total, 3%, taxable Yes) auto-applies.
2. A work order exists whose net subtotal (after line-level adjustments) = $300.00 and pre-fee tax = $24.00 (so Grand Total base = $324.00).
column6:
1. Open the work order and read the Processing Fee amount.
2. Check it works out after all other fees/discounts.
column7:
1. The Processing Fee is +$9.72 (3% of $324.00).
2. It works out last, left out of its own base and every other Processing Fee's base.
3. If taxable, its $9.72 is added to the taxable amount but its own base does not change.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee with a Max Amount or a disallowed method is rejected
column5: 1. Ability to submit template data (via UI edge case or API) for a Processing Fee carrying a Max Amount, or a method other than Flat Amount / % of Grand Total.
column6:
1. Try to save a Processing Fee template that has a Max Amount.
2. Try to save a Processing Fee with a method other than Flat Amount or % of Grand Total (for example % of Subtotal).
column7:
1. Both are rejected.
2. A Processing Fee can only be Flat Amount or % of Grand Total and never has a Max Amount.

column1: Verify a Processing Fee always adds to the total (never a discount)
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template exists and is on a WO.
column6:
1. In the template dialog, confirm there is no way to make a Processing Fee a discount.
2. On the work order, confirm the amount has a plus (+) sign.
column7:
1. A Processing Fee always works out to a plus (+) amount; it can never be a discount.
2. There is no 'Processing Discount' type.

column1: Verify editing a Processing Fee template does not change Processing Fees already on existing work orders
column5: 1. A Processing Fee template auto-applied to an existing OPEN work order (e.g. Flat $5.00).
column6:
1. Edit the Processing Fee template amount from $5.00 to $8.00 and save.
2. Open an existing work order and read its Processing Fee amount.
column7:
1. The existing work order's Processing Fee still shows $5.00 (unchanged).
2. Only new work orders created after the edit use the $8.00 value.

column1: Verify multiple Processing Fees each leave out all Processing Fees' amounts and tax from the shared base
column5:
1. Two Processing Fee templates (both % of Grand Total) auto-apply to one work order.
2. Net subtotal $300.00, pre-fee tax $24.00 → Grand Total base $324.00.
column6:
1. Create a new work order so two Processing Fees apply.
2. Read each Processing Fee's amount.
column7:
1. Both Processing Fees work out against the same base (which excludes every Processing Fee's amount and tax).
2. Neither Processing Fee grows the other's base.

column1: Verify the system rejects a Processing Fee that carries a minimum amount
column5: 1. Ability to submit a Processing Fee with a non-empty minimum amount (no UI control exists; guard for external data).
column6: 1. Try to save a Processing Fee template that carries a minimum amount.
column7:
1. A Processing Fee does not support a minimum amount, and this is made clear rather than silently dropped: there is no minimum-amount field for a Processing Fee anywhere in the UI.
2. If a minimum (or maximum) amount is sent for a Processing Fee, the system rejects it with the explicit message 'A processing fee cannot have a minimum or maximum cap.'

column1: Verify one layout renders adjustments on both the estimate and the invoice
column5: 1. A work order has whole-WO and line-level adjustments and can produce both an estimate and an invoice.
column6:
1. View the customer ESTIMATE for the WO and note the adjustment rendering.
2. Invoice the WO and view the customer INVOICE.
column7:
1. Both the estimate and the invoice show the same adjustment layout.
2. Adjustments appear on both whenever present.

column1: Verify a labor-line percentage adjustment renders indented with ↳, the "(% of labor)" phrase, and correct amount sign
column5: 1. A WO has a labor line with a "Shop Supply Fee" (% of Labor Total, fee) and a labor-line discount.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Find the labor line and its adjustment rows.
column7:
1. The adjustment shows indented UNDER its labor line with a "↳" arrow before the name.
2. For the percentage fee the name is followed by the phrase "(% of labor)" (a phrase, not a number).
3. A fee amount shows as "$X.XX"; a discount amount shows in accounting brackets "($X.XX)" — two decimals, no minus sign.

column1: Verify a part-line adjustment renders with "(% of parts)" (percentage) and no phrase for Flat Amount
column5: 1. A WO part has a percentage part-line adjustment and another part has a Flat Amount part-line adjustment.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Inspect both part-line adjustment rows.
column7:
1. The percentage part-line adjustment shows the phrase "(% of parts)" after its name.
2. The Flat Amount adjustment shows NO bracketed phrase.

column1: Verify fee vs discount amount formatting (fee "$X.XX", discount "($X.XX)")
column5: 1. A WO has both a fee and a discount adjustment.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Compare the fee and discount amount cells (both per-line and in the bottom Adjustments block).
column7:
1. A fee amount reads "$X.XX" (e.g. "$3.75").
2. A discount amount reads "($X.XX)" in round accounting brackets (e.g. "($26.08)") — two decimals and NO minus sign.
3. Both the per-line rows and the bottom Adjustments block use the same format.

column1: Verify the bottom "Adjustments" block lists whole-WO adjustments one by one in creation order
column5: 1. A WO has 3 whole-WO adjustments created in a known order, including a % of Subtotal and a Flat Amount.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Find the "Adjustments" block near the bottom and read the order and labels.
column7:
1. A block titled "Adjustments" appears after Labor/Parts/Shop Supplies and before Subtotal (then Tax, then Total).
2. Whole-WO adjustments are listed one by one in CREATION order (oldest first).
3. Each percentage adjustment shows its phrase — one of "% of labor", "% of parts", "% of subtotal", or "% of grand total" (Processing Fee); a Flat Amount shows no phrase.

column1: Verify line-level adjustments are grouped by name+type in the bottom block with a "(×N)" count
column5: 1. A WO has three separate "Shop Supply Fee" line-level fees (same name+type) across different lines.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate/invoice.
2. Inspect the bottom "Adjustments" block.
column7:
1. The three same-named line-level fees are grouped into ONE row reading "Shop Supply Fee (×3)" with the total resolved amount.
2. Each of the three ALSO still shows inline under its own target line.

column1: Verify a % of Grand Total Processing Fee shows the "% of grand total" phrase on the document
column5: 1. A WO carries a % of Grand Total Processing Fee.
column6: 1. View the customer estimate/invoice bottom Adjustments block.
column7: 1. The Processing Fee row shows the phrase "% of grand total" after its name.

column1: Verify Shop Supplies is hidden on the estimate/invoice/financial tab when the total is $0.00
column5: 1. A WO whose total shop supplies = $0.00.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate, the invoice, and the financial tab.
2. Look for a Shop Supplies heading/line.
3. Also open the WO's left-side financial card.
column7:
1. When shop supplies = $0.00, the Shop Supplies header/contents do NOT display on the estimate, invoice, or financial tab.
2. Shop Supplies remains visible/modifiable in the WO left-side financial card (hidden only from the end-customer views).

column1: Verify Shop Supplies reappears on the customer views when its total becomes greater than $0.00
column5: 1. A WO that currently has $0.00 shop supplies (Shop Supplies hidden on customer views).
column6:
1. Add shop supplies so the total becomes > $0.00.
2. Re-view the estimate/invoice/financial tab.
column7: 1. Once shop supplies > $0.00, the Shop Supplies heading and contents become visible again on the customer-facing views.

column1: Verify a line-level adjustment on a not-billable (declined) line resolves to $0.00 but still shows
column5: 1. A WO labor line with an adjustment is set to declined/not-billable.
column6:
1. View the customer estimate (including a Needs Approval estimate).
2. Inspect the declined line's adjustment.
column7:
1. The adjustment resolves to $0.00 while the target is not billable, but still SHOWS wherever its target shows (including a Needs Approval estimate).
2. When the line becomes billable/authorized, the adjustment resolves to its non-zero amount.

column1: Verify the Adjustments block sits after Labor/Parts/Shop Supplies and before Subtotal → Tax → Total
column5: 1. A WO with labor, parts, shop supplies (> $0.00), and whole-WO adjustments.
column6: 1. View the customer estimate/invoice totals section from top to bottom.
column7: 1. Order is: Labor, Parts, Shop Supplies, then the "Adjustments" block, then Subtotal, then Tax, then Total.

column1: Verify each fee/discount exports to QuickBooks as its own invoice line item (fee adds, discount subtracts)
column5:
1. Location has an active QuickBooks connection with mapped Fee and Discount items.
2. A WO with one fee (+$10.00) and one discount (−$20.00) is invoiced.
column6:
1. Invoice the WO so it syncs to QuickBooks.
2. Inspect the QuickBooks invoice line items.
column7:
1. The fee is its own QuickBooks line item with a positive amount (+$10.00).
2. The discount is its own QuickBooks line item with a negative amount (−$20.00).
3. Each adjustment is a separate line (not merged into labor/parts).

column1: Verify the QuickBooks line description equals the fee/discount name and uses the mapped Fee/Discount item
column5:
1. QuickBooks connected with a mapped Fee item and Discount item.
2. A WO has a fee named "Hazmat Disposal Fee"; the WO is invoiced.
column6: 1. Inspect the synced QuickBooks line for the fee.
column7:
1. The QuickBooks line DESCRIPTION = "Hazmat Disposal Fee" (the adjustment name as shown on the customer invoice).
2. The Product/Service ITEM = the location's mapped Fee item (not the adjustment name).
3. A discount posts to the mapped Discount item likewise.

column1: Verify a $0.00 fee/discount is skipped when sent to QuickBooks
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; a WO has an adjustment that resolves to $0.00 (e.g. target not billable, or $0 base).
column6:
1. Invoice the WO and inspect the QuickBooks line items.
2. Also view the ShopView screens for the same adjustment.
column7:
1. The $0.00 adjustment is NOT sent as a QuickBooks line (skipped).
2. It still SHOWS as $0.00 on every other ShopView screen.

column1: Verify adding a fee is blocked when the Fee item is not mapped to QuickBooks
column5:
1. QuickBooks connected; the Fee item is NOT mapped in Settings → QuickBooks.
2. The Discount item IS mapped.
3. An open WO is available.
column6:
1. Open the WO toolbar ⋯ → "Add Work Order Fee / Discount", set Type = Fee, and try to save.
2. In the same dialog, set Type = Discount and try to save.
column7:
1. Saving a FEE is blocked with the message exactly: "Map a Fee item in Settings → QuickBooks before adding a fee." ("Settings → QuickBooks" is a link).
2. Saving a DISCOUNT succeeds (the block is per kind — only fees are blocked when the Fee item is missing).

column1: Verify adding a discount is blocked when the Discount item is not mapped to QuickBooks
column5:
1. QuickBooks connected; the Discount item is NOT mapped; the Fee item IS mapped.
2. An open WO is available.
column6:
1. Try to add a Discount to the WO.
2. Try to add a Fee to the WO.
column7:
1. Saving a DISCOUNT is blocked with the message exactly: "Map a Discount item in Settings → QuickBooks before adding a discount."
2. Saving a FEE succeeds (per-kind block).

column1: Verify the mapping block applies on every add place (work order, labor line, part, part sale, apply-from-template)
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; Fee item UNMAPPED.
column6: 1. Try to add a fee from: the WO dialog, a labor-line dialog, a part dialog, a part-sale whole-sale dialog and a single-part dialog, and by applying a fee template to a WO.
column7: 1. Every one of these add paths is blocked with the same "Map a Fee item in Settings → QuickBooks before adding a fee." message.

column1: Verify an auto-apply template cannot be saved while the matching QuickBooks item is not mapped
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected; Fee item UNMAPPED.
column6:
1. Try to mark a Fee template as auto-apply at the location.
2. Try to set a Fee template as a customer default.
column7:
1. Setting up an auto-apply Fee default (location auto-apply OR customer default) is BLOCKED while the Fee item is unmapped.
2. The block is at setup, so an auto-apply default never adds a fee on the server without a mapped item.

column1: Verify creating/editing a non-auto-apply template is always allowed, with no block when QuickBooks is not connected
column5: 1. Scenario A: QuickBooks connected with Fee item unmapped; scenario B: QuickBooks NOT connected.
column6:
1. Scenario A: create/edit a NON-auto-apply Fee template.
2. Scenario B (QuickBooks not connected): add a fee to a WO.
column7:
1. Scenario A: creating/editing a non-auto-apply template in Settings is always allowed (no block).
2. Scenario B: with QuickBooks not connected, there is no mapping block anywhere.

column1: Verify unmapping an in-use item sends affected invoices to Unexported Items (recoverable, no data lost)
column5: 1. QuickBooks connected with mapped Fee item; a WO with a fee is ready to invoice/sync.
column6:
1. Unmap the Fee item in Settings → QuickBooks (or connect QuickBooks after fees already exist).
2. Sync/invoice the affected WO.
3. Re-map the Fee item and re-export the invoice.
column7:
1. At sync time, each affected invoice goes to "Unexported Items" (not hard-blocked).
2. After re-mapping the item and re-exporting, the invoice exports; no data is lost.
3. The Settings → QuickBooks page prompts to map the Fee and Discount items, the same way it prompts for Credit and Deposit items.
